::: {.caveat-box}
**A note about the impact of under-identification**

`r note_box_underidentification`
:::

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>

::: {.key-question}
What health and wellbeing practices are Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples living in the NEPHU catchment engaging in?
:::

**Key points from stakeholder consultation**

- At stakeholder consultation during the development of this report the cost of living crisis was identified as a significant factor influencing these data, with concerns raised about vegetables being too expensive, while sugary drinks were relatively cheap.

- The data on sugary drinks was also likely to be an underestimation, with anecdotal reports of many people consuming them daily. In addition to being affordable, sugary drinks were seen as easily accessible enjoyment that is positive for wellbeing.

- An example of a local program addressing access to fruit and vegetables is the [Foodshare program](https://www.barrbuninbeek.org/programs) run by Barrbunin Beek Aboriginal Gathering Place, which provides weekly boxes of fruit and vegetables for pick-up.

## Fruit Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fruit consumption - meeting guidelines
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
fruit_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                              variable   = answer,
                              row_range  = 20:22) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Adults", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Met recommended fruit guideline"          ~ "Met guideline",
      answer == "Did not meet recommended fruit guideline" ~ "Did not meet guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                 ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

fruit_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                              variable   = answer,
                              row_range  = 7:9) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Children", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Met recommended fruit guideline"          ~ "Met guideline",
      answer == "Did not meet recommended fruit guideline" ~ "Did not meet guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                 ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

# Data wrangling
diet_fruit <- fruit_adult %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(fruit_child) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(answer,
                                levels = c("Met guideline",
                                           "Did not meet guideline",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fruit consumption - increase/decrease
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
fruit_increase <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Fruit_Increased.csv")

# Data wrangling
fruit_increase <- fruit_increase %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(increased_n:stayed_about_the_same_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(similar_n = stayed_about_the_same_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(increased_n:similar_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("increased"),
                starts_with("similar"),
                starts_with("decreased"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "increased" = "Increased",
                                              "similar"   = "Similar",
                                              "decreased" = "Decreased",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Increased",
                                           "Similar",
                                           "Decreased",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 26% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria met the daily fruit consumption guidelines, which [recommend a minimum number of daily serves](https://www.nhmrc.gov.au/adg) based on a person’s age and sex. This equates to approximately 12,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria.

- Overall, 58% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria met the daily fruit consumption guidelines. This equates to approximately 16,000 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria.

- Female survey respondents were more likely to have met the daily fruit consumption guidelines than males for both adults (29% vs. 23%) and children (63% vs. 56%).

- 18% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed more fruit at the time of the survey than they did at the same time in the previous year, and 65% reported that their level of fruit consumption was similar to the same time in the previous year.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to have increased their fruit consumption compared to the same time in the previous year than females (22% vs. 14%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- How many serves of fruit (including fresh, dried, frozen, and tinned) do you usually eat each day?
  - Numeric response (1-20)
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Since this time last year, has the amount of fruit you usually consume increased, decreased, or stayed about the same?
  - Increased
  - Decreased
  - Stayed about the same

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Vegetable Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vegetable consumption - meeting guidelines
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
vege_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                             variable   = answer,
                             row_range  = 24:26) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Adults", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Met recommended vegetable guideline"          ~ "Met guideline",
      answer == "Did not meet recommended vegetable guideline" ~ "Did not meet guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                     ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

vege_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                             variable   = answer,
                             row_range  = 11:13) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Children", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Met recommended vegetable guideline"          ~ "Met guideline",
      answer == "Did not meet recommended vegetable guideline" ~ "Did not meet guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                     ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

# Data wrangling
diet_vege <- vege_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(vege_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(answer,
                                levels = c("Met guideline",
                                           "Did not meet guideline",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vegetable consumption - increase/decrease
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
vege_increase <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Vegetable_Increased.csv")

# Data wrangling
vege_increase <- vege_increase %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(increased_n:stayed_about_the_same_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(similar_n = stayed_about_the_same_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(increased_n:similar_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("increased"),
                starts_with("similar"),
                starts_with("decreased"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "increased" = "Increased",
                                              "similar"   = "Similar",
                                              "decreased" = "Decreased",
                                              "answered"  = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Increased",
                                           "Similar",
                                           "Decreased",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 4.5% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria met the daily vegetable consumption guidelines which [recommend a minimum number of daily serves](https://www.nhmrc.gov.au/adg) based on a person’s age and sex. This equates to approximately 2,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Males were more likely to have met the guidelines than females (5.0% vs. 3.7%).

- Overall, 5.8% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria met the daily vegetable consumption guidelines. This equates to approximately 1,600 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Females were more likely to have met the guidelines than males (4.5 % vs. 2.9%).

- 15% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed more vegetables at the time of the survey than they did at the same time in the previous year, and 73% reported that their level of vegetable consumption was similar to the same time in the previous year.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to have increased their vegetable consumption compared to the same time in the previous year than females (18% vs. 10%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following questions were asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- How many serves of vegetables (including fresh, frozen, and tinned) do you usually eat each day?
  - Numeric response (1-20)
  
<div style="height: 1em;"></div>

- Since this time last year, has the amount of vegetables you usually consume increased, decreased, or stayed about the same?
  - Increased
  - Decreased
  - Stayed about the same

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::

## Sugar Sweetened Drinks Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sugar sweetened drinks consumption - weekly
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
sugar_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                              variable   = answer,
                              row_range  = 32:34) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Adults", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Usually consumes sugar sweetened drinks"         ~ "At least once per week",
      answer == "Does not usually consume sugar sweetened drinks" ~ "Less than once per week",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                        ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

sugar_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                              variable   = answer,
                              row_range  = 19:21) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Children", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Usually consumes sugar sweetened drinks"         ~ "At least once per week",
      answer == "Does not usually consume sugar sweetened drinks" ~ "Less than once per week",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")                        ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

# Data wrangling
drink_sugar <- sugar_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(sugar_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(answer,
                                levels = c("At least once per week",
                                           "Less than once per week",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sugar sweetened drinks consumption - daily
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
sugar_daily <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Drink_Sugar.csv")

# Data wrangling
sugar_daily <- sugar_daily %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(consumes_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n:does_not_consume_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(daily_n    = consumes_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n,
                notdaily_n = does_not_consume_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(daily_n:notdaily_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("daily"),
                starts_with("notdaily"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "daily"    = "Daily",
                                              "notdaily" = "Less than daily",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Daily",
                                           "Less than daily",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 59% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria consumed sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 29,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Males were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week than females (70% vs. 52%).

- Overall, 54% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria consumed sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 14,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Females were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week than males (62% vs. 47%).

- 22% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed sugar sweetened drinks daily.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks daily than females (30% vs. 13%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}

## Artifically Sweetened Drinks Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diet drinks consumption - weekly
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                             variable   = answer,
                             row_range  = 36:38) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Adults", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Usually consumes diet drinks"         ~ "At least once per week",
      answer == "Does not usually consume diet drinks" ~ "Less than once per week",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")             ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

diet_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                             variable   = answer,
                             row_range  = 23:25) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_group = "Children", .before = answer,
    #
    answer = dplyr::case_when(
      answer == "Usually consumes diet drinks"         ~ "At least once per week",
      answer == "Does not usually consume diet drinks" ~ "Less than once per week",
      stringr::str_detect(answer, "Total")             ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ answer))

# Data wrangling
drink_diet <- diet_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(diet_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(answer,
                                levels = c("At least once per week",
                                           "Less than once per week",
                                           "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diet drinks consumption - daily
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_daily <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Drink_Diet.csv")

# Data wrangling
diet_daily <- diet_daily %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(consumes_diet_drinks_daily_n:does_not_consume_diet_drinks_daily_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(daily_n    = consumes_diet_drinks_daily_n,
                notdaily_n = does_not_consume_diet_drinks_daily_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(daily_n:notdaily_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("daily"),
                starts_with("notdaily"),
                starts_with("answered")) %>% 
  #
  tidyr::pivot_longer(!sex,
                      names_to = c("answer", ".value"),
                      names_pattern = "(.+)_(.+)") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(answer = factor(dplyr::recode(answer,
                                              "daily"    = "Daily",
                                              "notdaily" = "Less than daily",
                                              "answered" = "Total"),
                                levels = c("Daily",
                                           "Less than daily",
                                           "Total")))
```

- Data for this topic were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 34% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria consumed artificially sweetened (diet) drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 16,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Females were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week than males (38% vs. 29%).

- Overall, 19% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria consumed artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 5,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Males were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week than females (18% vs. 15%).

- 8.1% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed artificially sweetened drinks daily.

- Female survey respondents were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks daily than males (11% vs. 4.9%).

::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" icon=false collapse=false}
The following question was asked of all people completing the 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey.

- On average, on how many days per week do you usually drink diet soft drink, cordials, sports drinks, or caffeinated energy drinks? These are drinks that have artificial sweeteners (e.g. saccharin, aspartame, sucralose) added to them rather than sugar.
  - Numeric response (0-7)

<div style="height: 2em;"></div>
:::
